question_record.context: A recent security incident on the host `mb-adfs` involved multiple malicious activities. Initially, the system executable `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe` was renamed and launched, potentially by an attacker aiming to run malicious code or connect to an attacker-controlled network address while avoiding certain behavior-based detection technologies. The process is associated with the account `SYSTEM` with SID `S-2-2-78`.
question_record.question: Who is the account associated with the process that accessed the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe) memory?
solution: A renamed executable file `powershell.exe` was launched.
The account `bjenkins` was involved in a sensitive credential memory read from the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe).

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

67.name: Sensitive credential memory read
67.description: A process scanned or dumped memory from the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe).  Accessing this process memory allows the attacker to extract secrets such as authentication hashes or passwords.  A copy of this memory may be written to the file system and exfiltrated to extract these credentials offline.
